﴿And whoever of you turns back from his religion and dies while a disbeliever, those are the ones whose deeds have become void﴾: he restricted apostasy by death upon it for the nullification of deeds, as is the position of al-Shafiʿi, may God have mercy on him, and what is meant by deeds is the beneficial deeds. It has also been read as ḥabaṭat (حَبَطَتْ) with a fatḥa, and that is a dialect of the same word. ﴿In this world﴾, because what they imagined is invalid and what Islam holds of worldly and otherworldly benefits is lost, by the forfeiture of reward. ﴿And those are the companions of the Fire; therein they will abide forever﴾, like the rest of the disbelievers.

Indeed, those who believed [Quran 2:218 opening phrase] — it was also revealed concerning the companions of the expedition (sariyyah), when it was suspected of them that if they were spared from sin, they would have no reward.

﴿And those who emigrated and strove in the way of God﴾ — he repeated the relative pronoun to magnify emigration (hijrah) and struggle (jihad), as if the two were independent in achieving the hope. ﴿Those hope for the mercy of God﴾ — that is, His reward. He affirmed hope for them, indicating that deeds are neither obligatory nor decisive in proof, especially since the consideration is in the endings (al-khawatim). ﴿And God is Forgiving﴾ — for what they did in error and lack of caution. ﴿Merciful﴾ — by bestowing abundant reward and recompense.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 219:

﴿They ask you about wine and gambling.﴾ «It is narrated that there was revealed in Mecca His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And from the fruits of the date-palms and grapes you take from them intoxicant and good provision﴾, so the Muslims began to drink it. Then ʿUmar, Muʿadh, and a group of the Companions said: "Give us a ruling, O Messenger of God, concerning wine, for it takes away the intellect and strips away wealth." So this verse was revealed, and some drank it while others abstained. Then ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf invited some people among them, and they drank and became intoxicated. One of them led the prayer and recited: "Say, O disbelievers, I worship what you worship," so the verse was revealed: ﴿Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾, and few then drank it. Then ʿUtban ibn Malik invited Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas along with a group, and when they became intoxicated they boasted and recited poetry to one another. Saʿd recited a poem containing satire of the Ansar, so an Ansari struck him with the jawbone of a camel and wounded his head. He complained to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "O God, make clear to us a healing clarification regarding wine." Then this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, wine and gambling﴾ up to His saying: ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "We have desisted, O Lord."》 Wine (khamr) originally is a verbal noun from "khamara-hu," meaning he covered it (sataraho). The juice of grapes and dates when it becomes strong and foams is called by it, as if it covers the intellect. Likewise it is called intoxicant (sakar) because it intoxicates, i.e., it restrains (yahjizu) the intellect. It is forbidden absolutely, and likewise every intoxicant according to the majority of scholars. Abu Hanifa, may God Most High have mercy on him, said: the infusion of raisins and dates, when it is boiled until two-thirds of it has gone and then it becomes strong, its drinking is permitted as long as it does not intoxicate.

﴿And gambling (maysir)﴾ is also a verbal noun like "mawʿid." Gambling (qimar) is called by it because it is taking the property of another by ease, or stripping away his ease (yasar). The meaning is: they ask you about engaging in both of them, based on His saying: ﴿Say: In both of them﴾, i.e., in engaging in them. ﴿There is great sin﴾ insofar as it leads to abandoning what is commanded and committing what is prohibited. Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "kathir" (great) with the letter thāʾ. ﴿And benefits for people﴾ in gaining wealth, pleasure and delight, and companionship of young men; and in wine especially, encouraging the coward, providing manliness, and strengthening the nature. ﴿And their sin is greater than their benefit﴾, i.e., the corruptions that arise from them are greater than the benefits expected from them. For this reason it has been said that this verse is the one that prohibits wine, because when corruption outweighs benefit, it necessitates the prohibition of the act. The more evident view is that it is not so, for what has passed concerning the refutation of the doctrine of the Mu'tazila.

﴿And they ask you what they should spend﴾. It has been said that its questioner was also ʿAmr ibn al-Jamuh; he first asked about what is spent and where it goes, then asked about the manner of spending. ﴿Say: the surplus (al-ʿafw)﴾. Al-ʿafw is the opposite of exertion (al-juhd), and from it is said of easy land; it is that one spends what is easy for him to give and does not reach exertion in it.

He said:

"Take the surplus from me, that you may keep my affection; and do not speak in my anger when I am wrathful."

It is narrated that a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with a golden egg he had obtained in some of the spoils and said: "Take it from me as charity." The Prophet (ﷺ) turned away from him until he repeated it many times. Then he said, "Bring it," angrily. So he took it and threw it with such force that, had it struck him, it would have wounded him. Then he said: "One of you comes with all his wealth, gives it all in charity, and then sits begging of people. Charity is only what is given out of surplus wealth." Abu ʿAmr read "al-ʿafw" with a nominative vowel (rafʿ). ﴿Thus God makes clear to you the signs﴾, i.e., just as He made clear that surplus is better than exertion, or the rulings He mentioned. The kaf is in the accusative position as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, i.e., a clarification like this clarification. He used the singular for the sign though it is addressed to a plural, according to the interpretation of "group" and "collectivity." ﴿That you may give thought﴾ to the proofs and rulings.

in this world and the Hereafter, that is, in the affairs of both abodes, so that you take what is best and most beneficial in them, and avoid what harms you and does not benefit you, or what harms you more than it benefits you. ﴿And they ask you about orphans.﴾ When the verse ﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly...﴾ was revealed, they withdrew from the orphans, from mixing with them and from concern for their affairs, and that was hard on them. This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and then it was revealed: ﴿Say: Reforming them is good.﴾ That is, to involve yourselves with them for their reform, or the reform of their property, is better than keeping away from them. ﴿And if you mix with them, they are your brothers.﴾ This is an exhortation to mixing with them: that is, they are your brothers in religion, and it is the right of a brother to mix with his brother. It was also said that the meaning of "mixing" here is intermarriage. ﴿And Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer.﴾ This is a warning and a promise to those who mix with them, whether for corruption or for reform: that is, He knows their condition and will repay them for it. ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have burdened you.﴾ That is, if Allah had willed to cause you hardship (ʿanat), He would have burdened you, that is, imposed upon you what is difficult, from ʿanat, which is hardship, and He would not have permitted you to mix with them. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Mighty﴾, dominant, able to cause hardship. ﴿Wise﴾, He judges what wisdom requires and what capacity can bear.

(p-139)﴿And do not marry female idolaters until they believe﴾. That is, do not marry them. It is also read with a ḍamma (tunkiḥū, "do not give them in marriage"), meaning do not marry them off to Muslim men. The term "female idolaters" (al-mushrikāt) includes the women of the People of the Book (ahl al-kitāb, those who received earlier scripture), because the People of the Book are idolaters, as shown by His saying: ﴿The Jews say, "Ezra is the son of God," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of God." … Exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾. However, they are excluded from this ruling by His saying: ﴿And the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture﴾. "It was narrated that upon him be blessings and peace sent Marthad al-Ghanawi to Mecca to bring out some Muslims from it. A woman called ʿAnāq, whom he had loved in the pre-Islamic period, came to him and said, 'Will you not be alone with me?' He said, 'Islam has come between us.' She said, 'Would you like to marry me?' He said, 'Yes, but I must consult the Messenger of God ﷺ.' So he consulted him." Then the verse was revealed: ﴿And a believing slave-woman is better than a free idolatress﴾. That is, a believing woman, whether free or a slave, for all people are the servants and bondmaids of God. ﴿Even though she pleases you﴾ by her beauty and her qualities. The waw here is for the circumstantial clause, and "even though" (law) is used in the sense of "if," which is common. ﴿And do not marry male idolaters until they believe﴾: do not give believing women in marriage to them until they believe. This is general in its application. ﴿And a believing slave is better than an idolater, even though he pleases you﴾: this is a reason for the prohibition on forming alliances with them, and an encouragement to form alliances with believers. ﴿Those﴾ refers to the idolaters and idolatresses mentioned. ﴿Call to the Fire﴾: that is, to disbelief, which leads to the Fire, so their friendship and intermarriage are not fitting. ﴿And God﴾: that is, and His allies, meaning the believers. The genitive noun has been omitted and the noun in the genitive has been put in its place, to honour their status. ﴿Calls to Paradise and forgiveness﴾: that is, to belief and action which lead to them, so they are the most deserving of alliance. ﴿By His leave﴾: that is, by God's grace and facilitation, or by His decree and will. ﴿And He makes His signs clear to people that they may remember﴾: so that they may remember, or so that they may be in a state in which remembrance is expected of them, due to the inclination toward good and opposition to desire that He placed in the minds.

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 222:**

﴿They ask you about menstruation.﴾ It is narrated that (the people of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) would not live with menstruating women nor eat with them, like the practice of the Jews and the Magians (Majus), and this continued until Abu al-Dahdah (Abu al-Dahdah) asked about this, along with a group of the Companions (Sahabah), and then it was revealed.) The word al-mahid (المحيض) is a verbal noun (masdar), like al-maji' (المجيء) and al-mabit (المبيت). Perhaps the reason that He, glorified and exalted is He, mentioned "yas'alunaka" (يسألونك) without a conjunction (waw) three times, and then with it three times, is that the first questions were asked at different times, while the last three were asked at one time, so He mentioned them with the conjunction of collection (harf al-jam').

﴿Say: It is a harm.﴾ That is, menstruation is a filthy thing that harms whoever approaches it, through aversion to it.

﴿So keep away from women during menstruation.﴾ That is, abstain from having intercourse with them, due to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "You have only been commanded to keep away from intercourse with them when they menstruate, and He has not commanded you to expel them from the houses, as the non-Arabs do." This is the moderate course between the excess of the Jews and the negligence of the Christians, for they would have intercourse with them and not care about menstruation.

The description of it as a harm, and the ruling being built upon it with the particle fa' (فاء), indicates that it is the effective cause ('illah) of the ruling.

﴿And do not approach them until they become clean.﴾ This is an emphasis on the ruling and a clarification of its limit, which is that they wash themselves after the cessation of bleeding. This is clearly indicated by the recitation (qira'ah) of Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Asim, in the narration of Ibn Abbas, "yattahharna" (يَطَّهَّرْنَ), meaning "yatatahharna" (يَتَطَهَّرْنَ), in the sense of "yaghtasilna" (يَغْتَسِلْنَ), "they wash." It also agrees with His saying: ﴿Then when they have purified themselves, go to them﴾, for this requires that the permissibility of intercourse be delayed until after the washing (ghusl). Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, said: if she becomes clean for the majority of the menstrual period, it is permissible to approach her before washing.

﴿From where Allah has commanded you.﴾ That is, the place of approach that Allah has commanded you with and made lawful for you.

﴿Indeed Allah loves those who are constantly repentant﴾ from sins.

﴿And He loves those who purify themselves﴾ That is, those who keep themselves far from immoralities and filth, such as having intercourse with a menstruating woman and approaching in other than the lawful place.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 223:

﴿Your women are a tilth for you﴾ meaning places of tilling for you. He likened them to tilth because of the sperm-drops that are cast into their wombs, which resemble seeds. ﴿So go to your tilth﴾ that is, go to them as you go to the places of tilling. This serves as an explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So go to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾ (p-140) ﴿as you wish﴾, from whatever direction you wish. «It was narrated that the Jews used to say: "Whoever has intercourse with his wife from behind, into her vagina, will have a child who is cross-eyed." This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and so this was revealed.» ﴿And put forward for yourselves﴾ what is stored up for you of reward. It was said it means seeking offspring. It was said it means saying the name of Allah at the time of intercourse. ﴿And fear Allah﴾ by avoiding His disobediences. ﴿And know that you will meet Him﴾ so provide yourselves with what will not disgrace you. ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾ who are perfect in faith, of honour and everlasting bliss. The Messenger (ﷺ) was commanded to advise them and to give good tidings to those among them who affirmed him and obeyed his command.

The verse: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle through your oaths, that you should not be righteous and God-fearing and make peace between people﴾. It was revealed concerning al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) when he swore that he would no longer spend on Mistah because of his slander against Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her). Another report says it was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Rawahah, who swore that he would not speak to his brother-in-law Bashir ibn al-Nu'man and would not reconcile between him and his sister.

Al-'urdah (on the pattern fu'lah in the sense of maf'ul, "that which is placed") is like qabdah (a handful). It is used both for what is placed in front of something to block it, and for the one exposed to a matter. According to the first sense, the meaning is: do not make Allah a barrier against what you have sworn to do of good works. Thus al-ayman ("oaths") here means the matters sworn about, as in the words of the Prophet (ﷺ) to Ibn Samurah: "If you swear an oath and then see something else to be better than it, then do what is better and make expiation for your oath." Upon him be prayers and peace.

Anna with its complement is an explicative apposition ('atf bayan, a noun clause that clarifies the preceding noun) for it. The lam is connected to ﴿obstacle﴾ because of the sense of opposition within it. It may also be causal (li al-ta'lil, expressing reason), and then anna is governed either by the verb or by 'urdah. That is: do not make Allah an obstacle so that you would be righteous, for the sake of your oaths by Him. According to the second sense: do not make Him an exposed target for your oaths, thereby cheapening Him through frequent swearing by Him. For this reason He censured the frequent swearer, saying: ﴿And do not obey every contemptible frequent swearer﴾. And ﴿that you should be righteous﴾ is the reason ('illah, cause) for the prohibition; that is, I forbid you from it intending your righteousness, your God-fearing, and your making peace between people. For the frequent swearer is bold against Allah, and one who is bold against Him is not righteous, God-fearing, or trusted in reconciling between people. ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of your oaths, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of your intentions.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 225:

﴿God will not take you to task for what is unintended in your oaths﴾. Al-laghw (that which is idle, meaning what is discarded and not regarded as valid, whether in speech or otherwise). The idle oath (laghw al-yamin) is that which has no binding intention behind it, such as when the tongue utters it by slip, or one speaks it while ignorant of its meaning, like the saying of the Arabs: "No, by God," and "Yes, by God," merely for emphasis. This is in line with His saying: ﴿But He will take you to task for what your hearts have earned﴾. The meaning is: God will not take you to task with punishment or expiation for what has no intention behind it; but He will take you to task for both, or for one of them, for what you intended of oaths and in which your hearts agreed with your tongues. Abu Hanifa said: al-laghw is that a man swears on the basis of his false supposition, and the meaning is: He will not punish you for what you erred in regarding oaths, but He will punish you for what you deliberately lied about. ﴿And God is Forgiving﴾ in that He did not take to task for the idle oath, ﴿Forbearing﴾ in that He did not hasten the taking to task for the oath of seriousness, giving time for repentance.

(p-141)

﴿For those who take an oath to abstain from their wives﴾ — that is, who swear that they will not have intercourse with them. Al-iilaa' (oath of abstention) means the oath; it takes the preposition ʿalā, but since this oath includes the meaning of keeping away, it is construed with min. ﴿A waiting period of four months﴾ — this is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is what precedes it, or it is the agent of the adverbial phrase, contrary to what precedes. At-tarabbus means waiting and pausing; it is annexed to the time-expression by way of extension (ittisaʿ), meaning that the husband has the right to delay during this period, so he is not pressed for a return (fayʾ) or for divorce. For this reason al-Shafiʿi said: there is no iilaa' except when it exceeds four months, and this is supported by ﴿but if they return﴾ — that is, they go back on the oath by breaking it — ﴿then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, All-Merciful﴾ — toward the husband for the sin of breaking his oath if he makes expiation, or for what he intended by the iilaa' of harming the woman and the like, with the return (fayʾah) which is like repentance.

﴿And if they resolve on divorce﴾ — and if they firmly determine its intention — ﴿then surely Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of their divorce, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of their purpose in it.

Abu Hanifa said: the iilaa' is for four months or more, and its ruling is that if the husband returns within the period by intercourse, if he is able, or by promise if he is unable, the return is valid, and the one who has intercourse is obliged to make expiation; otherwise she is separated from him after the period by one revocable divorce. According to us, after the period he is pressed to choose one of the two matters; if he refuses both, the judge divorces her on his behalf.

(p-141)

﴿For those who take an oath to abstain from their wives﴾ — that is, who swear that they will not have intercourse with them. Al-iilaa' (oath of abstention) means the oath; it takes the preposition ʿalā, but since this oath includes the meaning of keeping away, it is construed with min. ﴿A waiting period of four months﴾ — this is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is what precedes it, or it is the agent of the adverbial phrase, contrary to what precedes. At-tarabbus means waiting and pausing; it is annexed to the time-expression by way of extension (ittisaʿ), meaning that the husband has the right to delay during this period, so he is not pressed for a return (fayʾ) or for divorce. For this reason al-Shafiʿi said: there is no iilaa' except when it exceeds four months, and this is supported by ﴿but if they return﴾ — that is, they go back on the oath by breaking it — ﴿then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, All-Merciful﴾ — toward the husband for the sin of breaking his oath if he makes expiation, or for what he intended by the iilaa' of harming the woman and the like, with the return (fayʾah) which is like repentance.

﴿And if they resolve on divorce﴾ — and if they firmly determine its intention — ﴿then surely Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of their divorce, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of their purpose in it.

Abu Hanifa said: the iilaa' is for four months or more, and its ruling is that if the husband returns within the period by intercourse, if he is able, or by promise if he is unable, the return is valid, and the one who has intercourse is obliged to make expiation; otherwise she is separated from him after the period by one revocable divorce. According to us, after the period he is pressed to choose one of the two matters; if he refuses both, the judge divorces her on his behalf.

﴿The divorced women﴾: by them he means those who have been consummated with and who have menstrual periods (dhawat al-iqra'), because the verses and reports indicate that the ruling for other women is different from what is mentioned. ﴿Shall wait﴾ is a report in the sense of a command, and the change of expression is for emphasis and to signal that it is something one must hasten to obey. It is as if the addressee intended to comply with the command and so reports it, like your saying in a supplication: May Allah have mercy on you. Its being framed as a nominal sentence (mubtada') adds further emphasis. ﴿Themselves﴾ is an incitement and urging of them to wait, for women's souls yearn toward men, so they are commanded to restrain them and compel them to wait. ﴿Three quru'﴾ is in the accusative as an adverb of time (zarf) or as an object (maf'ul bihi), meaning: they shall wait out its duration.

Quru' is the plural of qur' (the menstrual period, or the interval of purity), which is used for menstruation, as in the words of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Leave off prayer during the days of your quru'."

It is also used for the period of purity between two menstrual periods, as in the words of al-A'sha:

"Inheriting wealth, and there is esteem in the tribe, for what was lost in them of your women's quru'."

Its original meaning is the transition from purity to menstruation, and this is what is meant in the verse, because it is what indicates the cleansing of the womb, not menstruation itself. This is what the Hanafis say, based on the saying of God Most High: ﴿so divorce them for their waiting period﴾, that is, at the time of their waiting period. A legally prescribed divorce does not occur during menstruation. As for the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The divorce of a slave woman is two pronouncements, and her 'iddah is two menstrual periods," it does not withstand what al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated in the story of Ibn 'Umar: "Order him to take her back, then let him keep her until she becomes pure, then she menstruates, then she becomes pure; then, if he wishes, he may keep her thereafter, and if he wishes, he may divorce her before he touches her. That is the 'iddah for which God Most High commanded that women be divorced."

By analogy it should have been expressed in the form of the paucity pattern, which is al-aqra' (the plural used for small numbers), but they use the forms broadly, employing each of the two patterns in place of the other. Perhaps, since the ruling covers all divorced women who have quru', it came to include the meaning of abundance, so its pattern (quru') was appropriate.

﴿And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs﴾: that is, the child, or the menstruation, in haste to end the 'iddah and to nullify the right of raj'ah (taking the wife back). This indicates that her word is accepted in this matter. ﴿If they believe in God and the Last Day﴾: its purpose is not to restrict the prohibition of concealment to their being believers. Rather, it is a warning that concealment contradicts faith, and that a believer does not dare to do it and it is not fitting for him to do so.

﴿And their husbands﴾: that is, the husbands of the divorced women. ﴿Have more right to take them back﴾: to marriage and to resuming them. However, this applies when the divorce is revocable (raj'i), by reason of the verse that follows. The pronoun is more specific than its antecedent, and there is no impediment to this, just as if one repeats a noun and specifies it.

Bu'ulah is the plural of ba'l, and the ta' is for the feminine form of the plural, like 'umumah and khu'ulah. Alternatively, it is a verbal noun from your saying ba'l husn al-bu'ulah (a husband good in marital relations), used as an adjective. Or it stands in place of an omitted possessed noun, meaning: and the people of their husbands. Af'al here has the meaning of the active participle (fa'il). ﴿In that﴾: that is, during the period of waiting. ﴿If they desire reconciliation﴾: by taking them back, not to harm the woman. The purpose is not to make intention for reconciliation a condition for taking back, but rather to encourage it and to prohibit the intention of harm.

﴿And women have rights similar to those they have, according to what is reasonable﴾: that is, women have rights over men similar to men's rights over them, in terms of obligation and the entitlement to demand them from the other party, not in kind. ﴿But men have a degree over them﴾: an increase in right and a superiority in it, because men's rights are over themselves, while women's rights are the dower, sustenance, and the avoidance of harm and the like. Or it means a nobility and excellence, since they are guardians (qiwam) over women and their protectors, sharing with them in the purpose of marriage, and they are singled out for the excellence of providing care and maintenance. ﴿And God is Mighty﴾: capable of exacting retribution from whoever opposes the rulings. ﴿Wise﴾: He legislates them for wisdoms and benefits.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 229:

﴿The divorce is twice﴾, i.e., revocable divorce (al-taṭlīq al-rajʿī) is twice, on the basis of what has been related: "(He ﷺ was asked, 'Where is the third?' And he, upon him be prayer and peace, said: ﴿Or release with kindness﴾.)" It has also been said that its meaning is lawful divorce (al-taṭlīq al-shar'ī), one pronouncement after another, separately, and for this reason the Ḥanafīs said: combining two or three pronouncements together is a bid'ah (innovation). ﴿Then retain in good manner﴾, by taking her back and treating her well, and this supports the first meaning. ﴿Or release with kindness﴾, by the third pronouncement, or by not taking her back until she is separated. On the last meaning, it is a ruling of a new subject and an unrestricted option, after which he goes on to teach them the manner of divorce. ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them﴾, i.e., of the dowries.

It has been related: "(That Jamīlah bint ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl used to hate her husband Thābit ibn Qays, so she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: 'Neither I nor Thābit! My head and his head will not be joined by anything. By Allah, I do not fault him in religion or character, but I dislike disbelief in Islam, and I cannot bear him.' She said: 'I lifted the side of the tent and saw him coming in a group of men, and he was the darkest of them, the shortest of stature, and the ugliest of face.') Then it was revealed, and she obtained a khul‘ (divorce for compensation) from him with the garden which he had given her as dower."

The address is to the rulers (al-ḥukkām), and the attribution of taking and giving to them is because they are the ones who command both when there is litigation. It has also been said that the address is to the husbands, and what follows is an address to the rulers, but this disturbs the arrangement of the text according to the well-known reading. ﴿Unless they both fear﴾, i.e., the spouses. It has been read as "yaẓunnā" (they both suppose), and this supports interpreting fear as supposition. ﴿That they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾, i.e., abandon the establishment of His rulings, which are among the obligations of marriage. Ḥamzah and Yaʿqūb read "yakhāfā" in the passive voice, with "an" replacing its complement from the pronoun as a substitution of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl). It has been read as "takhāfā" and "tuqīmā" with the second-person ta. "If you (rulers) fear...": ﴿that they will not keep within the limits of Allah, then there is no blame upon them both regarding that by which she ransoms herself﴾, upon the man in taking what she ransoms herself with and divorces by it, and upon the woman in giving it. ﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾, a reference to the rulings He has set down. ﴿So do not transgress them﴾, i.e., do not overstep them by opposition. ﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah, those are the wrongdoers﴾, a consequence of the prohibition with a threat, for emphasis in warning. Know that the apparent meaning of the verse indicates that khul‘ is not permissible without aversion and discord, nor with everything the husband has given her, let alone the surplus, and this is supported by his saying ﷺ: "Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without cause, the fragrance of Paradise is forbidden to her."

And what has been related: "(That he, upon him be prayer and peace, said to Jamīlah: 'Will you return to him his garden?' She said: 'I will return it and add to it.' He, upon him be prayer and peace, said: 'As for the surplus, no.')" The majority disliked this but upheld it, since the prohibition of the contract does not indicate its invalidity, and it is valid with the wording of ransom (mufādāh), for He, exalted is He, named it ransom (iftidāʾ). It has been disputed whether, if it takes place without the wording of divorce, it is a annulment (faskh) or a divorce (ṭalāq); and whoever holds it to be an annulment argues with His saying:

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 230:

﴿Then if he divorces her﴾ For his following up the khul' (divorce by compensation, a wife's release from marriage in return for payment) after mentioning the two divorces requires that it be a fourth divorce, if khul' were a divorce.

The more apparent view is that it is a divorce, because it is a separation by the choice of the husband, so it is like divorce for a consideration. His words ﴿Then if he divorces her﴾ are connected to his words ﴿Divorce is twice﴾, or are an explanation of his words ﴿or release with kindness﴾, with the mention of khul' placed between them to indicate that divorce may occur without compensation at times and with compensation at other times. The meaning is: if he divorces her after the two. ﴿Then she is not lawful to him thereafter﴾ after that divorce. ﴿until she marries another husband﴾ until she marries someone other than him. Marriage (nikah) is attributed to each of the two (the contract and the consummation), as is the case with tazawwuj (to marry). Those who restricted it to its apparent meaning of the contract, such as Ibn al-Musayyib, relied on this, but the majority agreed that consummation is necessary, on the basis of what is related: "The wife of Rifa'ah said to the Messenger of God ﷺ: Indeed Rifa'ah divorced me and made my divorce final, and indeed 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr married me, and indeed what is with him is like the fringe of a garment. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: Do you want to return to Rifa'ah? She said: Yes. He said: No, until you taste his honey and he tastes yours." So the verse is general, and the Sunnah has restricted it. It is also possible that nikah is interpreted as consummation, and the contract is then derived from the word "husband". The wisdom of this ruling is to deter hastiness in divorce and to deter returning to a woman divorced three times, and to inculcate desire for her. A marriage on condition of tahlil (intended to make her lawful to the first husband) is invalid according to most scholars. Abu Hanifah permitted it with disapproval, but the Messenger of God ﷺ cursed "the one who performs tahlil and the one for whom tahlil is performed."

﴿Then if he (the second husband) divorces her﴾ ﴿there is no blame on them both if they return to each other﴾, that is, for the woman and the first husband each to return to the other by marriage, ﴿if they think that they will keep the limits of God﴾, that is, if in their assumption they will uphold what God has set as limits and prescribed of the rights of marriage. Interpreting "thinking" (zann) as "knowing" (ilm) here is not sound, because the outcomes of affairs are unseen and are only supposed, not known; and because one does not say "I know that Zayd will stand," since the particle "an" (that) governing the verb expresses expectation, which contradicts knowledge. ﴿And these are the limits of God﴾, that is, the rulings mentioned. ﴿He makes them clear to a people who know﴾, who understand, and who know in accordance with what knowledge requires.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 231:

﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term (ajal)﴾, i.e., the end of their waiting period ('iddah). The word ajal is used for a period of time and for its limit; it is said of a human being's lifespan and of the death by which it ends. He said:

"Every living being completes the term of its life,
and every person who is present departs when his term comes to an end."

Al-mulugh (reaching) is arrival at a thing, and it may be used, by extension, for approaching it; this is the meaning intended in the verse, so that the sense is correct or can be made to follow from it. ﴿Then retain them in kindness or release them in kindness﴾, since there is no retaining after the term has expired. The meaning is: take them back without harm, or leave them alone until their waiting period ends without prolonging it. This is a repetition of the ruling in one of its forms, for the sake of emphasis on it.

﴿And do not retain them to harm them﴾, that is, do not take them back intending to injure them. It is as if the divorcer leaves the woman in her waiting period until she nears the end of the term, then takes her back so that the waiting period will be prolonged for her. He is forbidden from this after being commanded to its opposite, for emphasis. Darar (harm) is in the accusative either as a reason (ʿillah) or as a circumstantial state (hal), meaning "harming them." ﴿So that you transgress﴾, that is, so that you wrong them by prolonging the term or by compelling them to ransom themselves (iftida'). The lam is connected to darar, since the intended meaning is to restrict it.

﴿And whoever does that has wronged himself﴾ by exposing himself to punishment. ﴿And do not take the signs of God in jest﴾, by turning away from them and being lax in acting upon what they contain. From their saying to one who does not earnestly pursue the matter: "You are only jesting," as if He forbade jesting and intended by it the opposite command. It was said: "A man would marry, divorce, and manumit, and say: 'I was only playing,'" and so this was revealed.

And from him, upon him be prayer and peace: "Three things, their earnest is earnest and their jest is earnest: divorce, marriage, and manumission."

﴿And remember the favor of God upon you﴾, among which is guidance and the sending of Muhammad (ﷺ), with gratitude and fulfilling its rights. ﴿And what He has sent down to you of the Book and wisdom﴾, the Qur'an and the Sunnah, which He singled out for mention to show their nobility. ﴿He admonishes you with it﴾, with what has been sent down to you. ﴿And fear God and know that God is Knowing of all things﴾: an affirmation and a warning.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 232:

﴿When you divorce women and they reach their term﴾, i.e., their waiting period (ʿiddah) has come to an end. Al-Shafiʿi (may Allah have mercy on him) said that the context of the two statements indicates that the two "reaching" (bulugh) are different. ﴿Do not prevent them from marrying their husbands﴾. The one addressed by this are the guardians (awliyaʾ), because of what has been narrated: (that it was revealed concerning Maʿqil ibn Yasar, when he prevented his sister Jumayla from returning to her first husband by a fresh marriage contract). Thus it is evidence that a woman does not contract her own marriage, for if she could do so there would be no meaning to the guardian's prevention. This is not contradicted by the attribution of the marriage to them (the women), because it is due to its dependence on their consent. It was also said that the husbands are meant, those who prevent their wives from marrying after the expiry of the waiting period, unjustly and by coercion, since it is the answer to His saying ﴿When you divorce women﴾. It was also said that they are the guardians and the husbands. It was also said that it is all people, and the meaning is: this matter should not be found among you; for when it is found among them, and they are content with it, they are the ones who do it. ʿAdl (prevention) means confinement and constriction, and from it comes "the hen became constricted (ʿadalat al-dajajah)" when her egg has lodged and she cannot expel it. ﴿When they agree among themselves﴾, i.e., the suitors and the women, and this is an adverbial clause (ẓarf) modifying either "they marry" or "do not prevent them". ﴿In a reasonable manner﴾: in what the Sharia recognizes and good manners approve; it is either a circumstantial qualifier of the implied subject of the verb, or an attribute of an omitted verbal noun, meaning: agreement that is in a reasonable manner. In it is evidence that preventing marriage to a non-equal (kafaʾah) is not forbidden. ﴿That﴾ refers to what has been mentioned before, and the address is to all in the sense of the group, or to each one, or the kaf is merely for address. The distinction between the near and the remote [demonstrative] is without specifying the addressees, or it is addressed to the Messenger (ﷺ) in the manner of His saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾, to indicate that the reality of what is referred to is something that almost no one can conceive.

﴿Whoever among you believes in Allah and the Last Day is admonished by it﴾, because he is the one who is admonished by it and benefits from it. ﴿That﴾, i.e., acting in accordance with what has been mentioned. ﴿Is more pure for you﴾: more beneficial. ﴿And more purifying﴾ from the filth of sins. ﴿And Allah knows﴾ what benefit and goodness is in it. ﴿And you do not know﴾ because of the deficiency of your knowledge.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (*Anwar al-Tanzil*) on surah 2, verse 233:

﴿The mothers shall breastfeed their children﴾ This is a command expressed in the form of a report, for emphasis. Its meaning is recommendation (*nadb*), or it may be obligation (*wujub*), in which case it applies only when the child will nurse only from its mother, or when no wet-nurse (*zi'r*) is available, or when the father is unable to hire one. The phrase ﴿the mothers﴾ includes divorced women and others. It has been said that it refers only to them, since the discussion concerns them. ﴿For two full years﴾ He emphasized this with the attribute of completeness, because it is something on which leniency is allowed. ﴿For whoever wishes to complete the nursing﴾ This clarifies the person addressed by the ruling, meaning: this applies to whoever wishes to complete the nursing. Or it is connected to ﴿shall breastfeed﴾, since the father is obliged to arrange nursing just as he is obliged to provide maintenance (*nafaqah*), and the mother nurses on his behalf. This is evidence that the maximum period of nursing is two years, that nothing after them is taken into account, and that it is permissible for it to be less than that. ﴿And upon the one to whom the child is born﴾ That is, the one to whom a child is born, meaning the father, since the child is born to him and is attributed to him. The change of expression points to the meaning that makes the nursing and the nursing mother's expenses incumbent upon him. ﴿Their provision and their clothing﴾ as a wage for them. Scholars differed regarding hiring the mother. Al-Shafi'i permitted it, while Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, prohibited it as long as she is a wife or in a waiting period of marriage (*mu'taddah nikah*). ﴿In a fair manner﴾ according to what the ruler (*al-hakim*) judges and what his capacity can meet. ﴿No soul is burdened except according to its capacity﴾ This is a justification for the obligation imposed on the believer, and the restriction to what is fair. It is evidence that He, glorified and exalted, does not burden a servant with what he cannot bear, and this does not preclude its possibility. ﴿No mother shall be harmed through her child, nor a father through his child﴾ This is an elaboration and confirmation of the previous statement, meaning: neither of them should burden the other with what is beyond his capacity, nor should harm be done to him because of the child. Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, and Ya'qub read ﴿lā tuḍārra﴾ with a *raf'* (nominative) as a substitute for the phrase ﴿lā tukallafu﴾. Its original form in both readings is *tuḍārir* with a kasra, in the active voice, or with a fatha, in the passive voice. According to the first form, it may mean "to harm" (*taḍurru*), with the *bā'* being part of its complement, meaning: the parents should not harm the child, so that they neglect his care and fall short in what is due to him. It has been read as ﴿lā tuḍārr﴾ with a sukun and shaddah, on the intention of pausing, and also with a light (*takhfif*) pronunciation as a verb from *ḍārrahu yuḍīruhu*. Mentioning the child's relation to the mother at one time and to the father at another is an appeal to them both and a reminder that the child deserves that they agree on his welfare and show concern for him, so they should not harm him, or harm one another because of him. ﴿And upon the heir is the like of that﴾ This is a conjunction with ﴿and upon the one to whom the child is born, their provision and their clothing﴾, and what lies between them is an intervening justification. By "the heir" is meant the heir of the father, namely the child, meaning the nursing mother's expenses are paid from his property if the father dies. It has been said that it refers to the surviving parents, based on the words of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, "and make him the heir among us". Both opinions agree with the school of al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, since according to him there is no maintenance except for the case of birth. It has been said that the heir is the child's heir. This was the view of Ibn Abi Layla. It has been said that his heir is his maḥram (unmarriageable relative), which is the position of Abu Hanifa. It has been said that they are his agnatic relatives (*'asabah*), and this was the view of Abu Zayd. The phrase ﴿that﴾ refers to what the father is obliged to provide in terms of food and clothing. ﴿But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation﴾ That is, weaning arising from mutual consent between them and consultation between them before the two years. Consultation, *mushawarah* and *mashwarah*, means seeking out an opinion, derived from *shurtu al-'asal*, when one extracts honey. ﴿Then there is no blame upon them both﴾ in that. The mutual consent of both is required out of concern for the child's welfare, and out of caution lest one of them act in a way that harms the child, for some purpose or other. ﴿And if you wish to seek wet-nurses for your children﴾ That is, to seek nurses for your children. It is said: "I made the woman nurse the child" (*arḍa'tu al-mar'ah al-ṭifl*), and "I asked her to nurse it for him" (*istarḍa'tuhā iyyāhu*), just as you say: "God granted my need" (*anjaḥa Allāhu ḥājatī*) and "I asked her to grant it for me" (*istanjaḥtuhu iyyāhā*). The first object is omitted because it is understood. ﴿Then there is no blame upon you﴾ in this. Its general application indicates that the husband may seek a nurse for the child and prevent the wife from nursing. ﴿When you hand over﴾ to the nurses. ﴿What you give﴾ what you intend to give as payment, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When you rise to prayer﴾. The reading of Ibn Kathir is "mā ataytum", from *atā* meaning to do a good deed, when one performs it. It has also been read as "ūtītum", meaning what God gave you and enabled you to pay of the wage. ﴿In a fair manner﴾ is connected to ﴿handed over﴾, meaning in the customary manner that is praiseworthy in the Law. The answer to the conditional is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. The condition of handing over is not a requirement for the permissibility of seeking a nurse, but rather for following what is better and more beneficial for the child. ﴿And fear God﴾ an emphasis on safeguarding what He has prescribed concerning children and nurses. ﴿And know that God, of what you do, is All-Seeing﴾ an exhortation and a warning.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 234:

﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, let the wives wait by themselves for four months and ten [days].﴾ That is, [the verse means] the wives of those who..., or: "Those of you who die and leave wives behind, let the wives wait after them," like their saying: "Ghee is two manans for a dirham" (a manan being a unit of weight). It is also read as "yatawaffawna" with a fatha on the ya (يَتَوَفَّوْنَ), meaning "they receive their full terms" (يَسْتَوْفُونَ آجالَهُمْ). The feminine form of "ashr" (عَشْرًا, ten) is used with reference to nights, because the nights are the beginnings of the months and days. For this reason they never use the masculine form in such a case, with reference to the days; so they say "ṣumtu ʿashran" (I fasted ten [days]). This is supported by His saying, ﴿You did not remain but ten [days]﴾, and then ﴿You did not remain but a day﴾. The likely basis for this estimate is that the fetus, in most cases, begins to move at three months if it is male, and at four months if it is female. So the longer of the two periods was taken, and ten [days] were added to it as a precaution, since its movement may be weak at the beginning and so not be felt. The general wording of the text requires that the Muslim woman and the People of the Book be equal in this ruling, as al-Shafiʿi said; and [that] the free woman and the slave woman [be equal], as al-Asamm said; and [that] the pregnant woman and others [be equal]. However, analogy (qiyas) required halving the period for the slave woman, and consensus (ijmaʿ) excluded the pregnant woman from this, based on His saying, ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾.

It is narrated from ʿAli and Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that she observes the longer of the two terms, as a precaution. ﴿Then when they have reached their term﴾, that is, when their waiting period has ended. ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, O rulers, or [O] Muslims all together, ﴿for what they do with themselves﴾, such as presenting themselves to suitors and other things that were forbidden to them during the waiting period. ﴿in accordance with what is reasonable﴾, in a manner that the Sharia does not reject. Its implication is that if they do what the Sharia rejects, then it is incumbent upon you to restrain them; if you fall short in this, then the blame is upon you. ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾, so He will reward you for it.

(p-146) ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you hint at in proposal to women﴾. Ta'ridh (allusion) and talwih (hinting) mean giving an impression of the intended meaning by means of something that has been coined neither literally nor figuratively, like the words of one who asks: "I have come to greet you." Kinayah (metonymy) is indicating a thing by mentioning its concomitants and attendants, like your saying of a tall man "tall of the sword-strap" (al-tawil al-nijad), and of a hospitable man "abundant in ashes" (kathir al-ramad). Al-khutbah (proposal), with a dammah or a kasrah, is a noun of state; however, the form with dammah is specific to a sermon, and the form with kasrah to a woman's proposal. What is meant by "women" here is women observing the waiting period for death. The allusion to proposing to her is that he says to her: "You are beautiful," or "You are a sought-after woman," or "I have a need to marry," and similar things. ﴿Or you conceal it within yourselves﴾, or you harbour it in your hearts without mentioning it, neither explicitly nor by allusion. ﴿God knows that you will remember them﴾ and that you will not be patient in refraining from mentioning them and from desiring them; and this contains a kind of rebuke. ﴿But do not make promises to them in secret﴾: this is a resumptive exception (istidrak) upon an elided element indicated by "you will remember them", meaning: so mention them, but do not make promises to them of marriage or intercourse. He expressed intercourse by "secret" because it is something kept private, and then marriage contract by it because it is a cause of it. It is also said that the meaning is: do not make promises to them in secret, with the sense that "promising in secret" means promising with what is shameful. ﴿Except that you say a fair word﴾, which is that you allude and do not state explicitly. The object of the exception is elided, i.e.: do not make them a promise except a well-known promise, or except a promise in fair words. It is also said that it is a disjunctive exception from ﴿secret﴾, but this is weak because it leads to your saying "do not promise them" except allusion, which is not a promise. In this is evidence for the prohibition of explicit proposal to a woman in the waiting period and the permissibility of alluding to her if she is in the waiting period for death. It is disputed regarding a woman in the waiting period of irrevocable divorce, and the more apparent view is that it is permissible. ﴿And do not resolve upon the tie of marriage﴾: he mentioned resolve (al-'azm) for emphasis in prohibiting the contract, i.e.: do not resolve to conclude the tie of marriage. It is also said the meaning is: do not sever the tie of marriage, for the original sense of 'azm is cutting. ﴿Until the decree reaches its term﴾: until what has been prescribed of the waiting period comes to its end. ﴿And know that God knows what is in your souls﴾ of resolve upon what is not permitted. ﴿So beware of Him﴾, and do not resolve. ﴿And know that God is Forgiving﴾ to one who resolved but did not act, out of fear of God, glorified and exalted is He. ﴿Forbearing﴾, He does not hasten to punish you.

**[Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on Surah 2, Verse 236]**

﴿There is no blame upon you﴾: no liability for a dower (*mahr*, the bridal gift). It is also said that it means no sin, because there is no innovation (*bid'ah*) in divorcing before consummation. It is also said that the Prophet ﷺ often forbade the roads (*turuq*, the paths), so he assumed there was hardship in this and negated it. ﴿If you divorce women while you have not yet touched them﴾: that is, have not had intercourse with them.

Hamza and al-Kisa'i read *tamassuhunna* (﴿touched them﴾) with a *ḍamma* on the *tā'* and a *madd* on the *mīm* throughout the Qur'an. ﴿Or you have not specified for them a portion﴾: this means "unless you specify," or "until you specify," or "and you specify." *Al-farḍ* means the specifying of the dower. *Farīḍatan* is in the accusative as the object (*maf'ūl bihi*). The form *fa'īla* carries the meaning of *maf'ūl*, and the *tā'* is for transferring the word from the adjectival to the nominal category. It may also be taken as a verbal noun (*maṣdar*). The meaning is that there is no liability on the one who divorces to pay the dower when the divorced woman has not been touched and no dower was specified. If she has been touched, then the obligation is the specified dower or the dower of the like (*mahr al-mithl*). If she has not been touched but a dower was specified, then she is owed half of the specified dower. Thus the explicit wording of the verse negates the obligation in the first case, and its implied meaning (*mafhūm*) requires the obligation in general in the latter two cases.

﴿And provide for them﴾: this is coordinated (*'aṭf*) with an implied element, meaning "so divorce them, and provide for them." The wisdom in making provision (*mut'ah*) obligatory is to remedy the distress caused by divorce. Its amount is left to the judgment of the judge (*ḥākim*). This is supported by His saying: ﴿The wealthy according to his means, and the straitened according to his means﴾, meaning each of the one who has ample means and the one whose means are restricted. *Al-muqtir* is one whose circumstances are constricted, and what he can afford and what is suitable for him. This is also indicated by the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to an Ansari man who divorced his wife, whom he had not specified a dower for, before touching her: "Provide for her with your cap." Abu Hanifa (may Allah be pleased with him) said: it is a shirt, a wrap, and a veil, according to the circumstances, unless the dower of her equivalent is less than that, in which case she is owed half the dower of the equivalent. The implied meaning of the verse requires restricting the obligation of provision to the woman for whom no dower was specified and whom the husband has not touched. Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him), in one of his two opinions, extended by analogy (*qiyas*) the touched woman for whom no dower was specified and the others to this ruling, and analogy takes precedence over the implied meaning.

Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Hafs, and Ibn Dhakwan read *matā'an* (﴿provision﴾) with a *fatḥa* on the *dāl* (*matā'an* as the verbal noun of *tamtī'*). ﴿According to what is fair﴾: in the manner that Sharia and common decency (*murū'ah*) approve. ﴿Due﴾: is an adjective of *matā'an*, or an emphatic verbal noun, meaning that this is due as a due. ﴿Upon the good-doers﴾: those who do good to themselves by hastening to obey, or to the divorced women by providing for them. He called them good-doers before the act because they are about to do it, as encouragement and incitement.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 237:

﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them, while you had already fixed for them a dower,﴾ Having mentioned the ruling on the *mufawwada* (the woman for whom no dower has been specified), he followed it with the ruling on its counterpart. ﴿then half of what you have fixed﴾, meaning: then for them (is half), or: what is obligatory is half of what you have fixed for them. This is evidence that the sin that was negated, then followed by the dower, and that there is no *mut'ah* (consolation gift) together with *tashtir* (halving the dower), because it is its counterpart. ﴿unless they forgo﴾, meaning the divorced women, so they take nothing. The verb form admits both the masculine and the feminine. The difference is that the *waw* in the first is a pronoun and the *nun* is the sign of the nominative, whereas in the second the *waw* is the *lam* of the verb and the *nun* is a pronoun, and the verb is *mabni* (indeclinable). For this reason, *an* (that) did not affect it here, and the word coordinated with it was put in the accusative. ﴿or he in whose hand is the knot of marriage forgoes﴾, meaning the husband, who holds the power over its contract and its dissolution, forgoes what would return to him through halving, so he gives her the full dower. This implies that divorce before *masis* (consummation) gives the husband a choice, and that it is not halved by itself. Some of our companions and the Hanafis held this view. It has also been said that it refers to the guardian who arranges their marriage, and that is when the woman is a minor. This is an old opinion of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him. ﴿And that you forgo is nearer to piety﴾ supports the first interpretation. The husband's forgoing, in the sense of choice, is clear. In the other interpretation it is an expression for giving more than what is due, and calling it "forgoing" is either by way of *mushakala* (wording by association) or because people used to hand the dower to the women at the time of marriage; so whoever divorces before consummation has the right to recover half, and if he does not recover it, he has forgiven it. It is narrated from Jubayr ibn Mut'im that he married a woman and divorced her before consummation, so he gave her the full dower and said: "I have more right to forgiveness." ﴿And do not forget graciousness between you﴾, meaning: and do not forget that some of you show favour to others. ﴿Indeed Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾, who does not waste your favour and your kindness.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 238:

﴿Guard well the prayers﴾ by performing them at their appointed times and by being constant in them. Perhaps the command to them is placed amid the rulings concerning children and spouses so that the preoccupation with their affairs does not distract them from it. ﴿And the middle prayer﴾: that is, the middle one among them (al-wusta, "the middle"), or the most excellent of them (al-fudla), and specifically it is the afternoon prayer (salat al-'asr).

This is based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) on the day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab): "They occupied us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer. May Allah fill their houses and graves with fire." It is given preference because people are much busy at its time, and because the angels gather (for it). It has also been said that it is the noon prayer (salat al-zuhr), because it falls in the middle of the day, and it was the most difficult of the prayers for them, so it was the most excellent, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The most excellent acts of worship are the most arduous of them." It has also been said that it is the dawn prayer (salat al-fajr), because it lies between the day prayers and the night prayers, and falls at the common boundary between them, and because it is witnessed. It has been said that it is the sunset prayer (salat al-maghrib), because it is the middle one in number and the odd (unit) of the day. It has been said that it is the night prayer (salat al-'isha'), because it lies between two audible prayers, falling at the two ends of the night.

It is related from 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite: "And the middle prayer, the prayer of the afternoon." So it becomes one of the four (prayers) singled out for mention together with the afternoon prayer, because these two are distinguished by excellence. It has also been read in the accusative (al-nasb), for specification and praise. ﴿And stand before Allah﴾ in prayer, ﴿devoutly obedient﴾, remembering Him while standing. Qunut is remembrance within it. It has been said it means humbly submissive. Ibn al-Musayyab said that what is meant by it is the qunut in the dawn prayer.

﴿فَإنْ خِفْتُمْ﴾ from an enemy or otherwise. ﴿فَرِجالا أوْ رُكْبانًا﴾ then pray on foot or riding. Rijal is the plural of راجِل (rajil, "one who is on foot"), or of رَجُل (rajul) with the same meaning, as in قائِم (qa'im) and قِيام (qiyam). This indicates that prayer is obligatory during the fighting (al-musayafah, "exchange of sword-blows"). Al-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him) held this view, while Abu Hanifah (may Allah have mercy on him) said: one does not pray while walking or fighting, unless it is standing (al-wuquf). ﴿فَإذا أمِنتُمْ﴾ and when you are secure and your fear has gone. ﴿فاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ pray the prayer of security, or give thanks to Him for the security. ﴿كَما عَلَّمَكُمْ﴾ with a remembrance like what He taught you of the laws and the manner of prayer in the two states of fear and security, or with a thanksgiving equal to it. Ma (ما) here is either a verbal-noun particle (masdariyyah) or a relative pronoun (mawsulah). ﴿ما لَمْ تَكُونُوا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ is the object of عَلَّمَكم (allamakum, "He taught you").

Commentary of al-Baydawi (*Anwar al-Tanzil*) on surah 2, verse 240:

﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind—a bequest for their wives﴾. Abu 'Amr, Ibn 'Amir, Hamza and Hafs, on the authority of 'Asim, read *wasiyyatan* in the accusative, on the assumed reading: "Those of you who die and leave wives behind should bequeath a bequest," or "let them bequeath a bequest," or "God has prescribed for them a bequest," or "I impose upon those who die a bequest." In support of this is the reading "God has prescribed for you the bequest for your wives, a provision until the year" in place of it.

The rest read it in the nominative, on the assumed reading: "and the bequest of those who die," or "and their ruling is a bequest," or "and those who die are people of a bequest," or "a bequest has been prescribed for them," or "a bequest is incumbent upon them." It was also read *matā'un* (nominative) in place of *wasiyyatun*.

﴿A provision until the year﴾ is in the accusative governed by *yūṣūna* (they bequeath) if that is taken as the implied verb; otherwise it is governed by *al-wasiyyah* (the bequest), or by *matā'an* on the reading of one who reads it so, because it carries the sense of providing enjoyment (*al-tamtī'*).

﴿Without eviction﴾ is either a substitute for it, or an emphatic infinitive like your saying "this statement is not what you say," or a circumstantial clause describing the wives, meaning "not being expelled." The meaning is: it is obligatory upon those who die to bequeath, before they are near death, that their wives be provided for after them for a year, with lodging and maintenance. This was at the beginning of Islam. Then the period was abrogated (*nusikha*, i.e., superseded by a later ruling) by His saying ﴿four months and ten days﴾. Although that verse comes earlier in the recitation, it was revealed later. The maintenance was dropped when the wife was assigned a quarter or an eighth as an inheritance. Her lodging, however, remains established for her according to us, in disagreement with Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him.

﴿But if they leave﴾ the marital home. ﴿Then there is no blame upon you﴾, O rulers. ﴿For what they do with themselves﴾, such as perfuming themselves and abandoning mourning (*al-iḥdād*, the mourning period). ﴿Of what is reasonable﴾, that which the Law has not disapproved. This indicates that it was not obligatory for her to remain in the husband's dwelling and to mourn for him; rather, she had the choice between remaining and taking maintenance, or leaving and forgoing it. ﴿And God is Mighty﴾, He takes vengeance upon whoever opposes Him among them. ﴿Wise﴾, He takes care of their interests.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 241–242:

﴿And for divorced women there is provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the God-conscious.﴾ He established the provision (mut'ah) for all divorced women after having made it obligatory for one of them. The singling out of some of the general (al-'amm) with a ruling does not specify it, except if we permit the specification of the explicit text (al-manṭūq) by the implicit meaning (al-mafhūm). Therefore Ibn Jubayr made it obligatory for every divorced woman, while others interpreted it to encompass both obligatory and recommended provision. Some people said that what is meant by the provision (matā') is the maintenance during the waiting period ('iddah). It is possible that the lam (in lil-muṭallaqāt) is for specification (al-'ahd), and the repetition is for emphasis, or for the recurrence of the matter. ﴿Thus﴾ is a reference to what preceded of the rulings concerning divorce and the waiting period. ﴿God makes clear to you His signs﴾ is a promise that He will make clear to His servants, from the proofs and rulings, what they need in their livelihood and their hereafter.

﴿So that you may understand﴾ means: so that you may comprehend them, and thus use your intellect (ʿaql) in them.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 243:

﴿Have you not seen﴾ is an expression of wonder and confirmation, addressed to those who heard their story from the People of the Book and the historians. It may also be addressed to one who neither saw nor heard it, since it has become a proverb for expressing wonder. ﴿Those who went out of their homes﴾ refers to the people of Dawardan, a village before Wasit, where a plague (ṭāʿūn) struck, so they fled. God caused them to die, then brought them back to life, so that they would take warning and be certain that there is no escape from the decree and predestination of God the Exalted. Or (it refers to) a people from the Children of Israel whom their king called to jihad, but they fled for fear of death, so God caused them to die for eight days, then brought them back to life. ﴿And they were thousands﴾ means many thousands. It is said ten thousand; it is said thirty thousand; it is said seventy thousand. It is also said they were ﴿muʾtalifūn﴾ (in the plural of ilf, or ālif, like qāʿid and quʿūd), and the wāw is for the circumstantial (ḥāl). ﴿For fear of death﴾ is an object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu). ﴿Then God said to them: "Die"﴾ means He said to them, "Die," and they died, like His saying: ﴿Be, and it is﴾. The meaning is that they died a single death, without any cause, by the command and will of God the Exalted. It is also said that an angel called out to them with this, and it is attributed to God the Exalted to instill fear and awe. ﴿Then He brought them back to life﴾ It is said: "Ḥizqīl, peace be upon him, passed by the people of Dawardan, whose bones had been laid bare and whose joints had come apart, so he marveled at that. God revealed to him, 'Call out to them that they should rise by the permission of God the Exalted,' so he called out and they rose, saying, 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; there is no god but You.'" The benefit of the story is to encourage the Muslims toward jihad and to face martyrdom, and to urge them to rely upon God and submit to His decree. ﴿Indeed, God is full of bounty toward mankind﴾ in that He brought them back to life so that they would take warning and prosper, and related their condition to them so that they would gain insight. ﴿But most people do not give thanks﴾ means they do not give thanks to Him as they should. It is permissible that by thanks is meant taking warning and gaining insight.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 244–245:

﴿And fight in the way of Allah﴾. When He explained that fleeing from death does not save one from it, and that what has been decreed is inevitably going to happen, He commanded them to fight, since if their term comes while they are in the way of Allah, that is better for them; otherwise there is victory and reward. ﴿And know that Allah is Hearing﴾ of what the one who stays behind and the one who hastens forward say, ﴿Knowing﴾ of what they conceal, and He is beyond (and behind) the recompense.

﴿Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan﴾. The particle مَن (man, "who") is an interrogative, in the nominative position by way of being the subject (mubtada'), with ذا (dha) as its predicate, and الَّذِي (alladhi) as an attribute (sifah) of ذا or as its substitute (badal). The lending to Allah, exalted is He, is a metaphor for presenting the deed by which its reward is sought. ﴿A goodly loan﴾: a lending that is goodly, accompanied by sincerity and a contented soul, or a lender who gives lawful and good (wealth). It has been said: the goodly loan is by striving and spending in the way of Allah. ﴿So that He may multiply it for him﴾: so that He multiplies its reward for him. He expressed it in the form of mughalabah (reciprocal contention) for the sake of emphasis. ʿĀṣim read فَيُضاعِفَهُ (fa-yudaʿifahu) with the accusative (naṣb), as a response to the interrogative, taking into account the meaning, since مَن ذا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ carries the sense of أيُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ أحَدٌ ("Does anyone lend to Allah?"). Ibn Kathir read فَيُضَعِّفُهُ (fa-yuḍaʿʿifuhu) with the nominative (raf') and doubling (tashdid), while Ibn ʿĀmir and Yaʿqub read it with the accusative. ﴿Manifold increases﴾: a multiplicity that none can measure except Allah, exalted is He. It has been said that one becomes seven hundred. Ḍiʿāfan (manifold) is the plural of ḍiʿf, and its accusative is either a state (ḥāl) of the accusative pronoun, or a second object (maf'ul thani) because the meaning of multiplying includes the meaning of making, or it is a verbal noun (maṣdar), since ḍiʿf is a verbal noun whose plural is used for variety. ﴿And Allah withholds and extends﴾: He restricts for some and widens for others according to what His wisdom requires. So do not be stingy toward Him with what He has widened for you, lest He change your state. Nafiʿ, al-Kisa'i, al-Bazzi and Abu Bakr read with the letter ṣād (يَصْبُطُ / ṣād form, i.e. "yaṣbuṭu"), and similarly in al-A'raf in His saying, ﴿And He increased you in stature, broadly﴾. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾, so He will recompense you according to what you have sent forward.
